The Emberá Dobidá, the river Emberá, are the Emberá who live along the rivers of the Chocó, the rainforest of western Colombia, especially the Atrato and San Juan basins. They speak an Emberá language of the small Chocoan family, shared with the mountain Eyábida and other Emberá.

They build houses on stilts by the water, travel by canoe, fish and grow plantains and maize, and paint their bodies with dark jagua dye. In colonial times the Spanish brought enslaved Africans to mine gold in the Chocó, and the Emberá moved upriver. Some later spread into Panama's Darién. In recent decades armed conflict has driven many from their land. Neighbours: Wounaan.
